questions.q: I *___* her yesterday at the station.
questions.explain: A finished time (*yesterday*) needs the past simple.

questions.q: I *___* here since 2018.
questions.explain: A situation from the past up to now, with *since*, takes the present perfect.

questions.q: I was cooking when the phone *___*.
questions.explain: A short action (past simple) interrupts a longer one in progress (past continuous).

questions.q: When we got to the cinema, the film *___*.
questions.explain: The past perfect shows an action before another past action.

questions.q: I *___* play football, but now I prefer tennis.
questions.explain: *used to* + base form describes a past habit that has stopped.

questions.q: I'm not used to *___* up so early.
questions.explain: In *be used to*, *to* is a preposition, so it's followed by *-ing*.

questions.q: Look at those black clouds! It *___* rain.
questions.explain: Predictions based on present evidence use *be going to*.

questions.q: "The doorbell's ringing." "I *___* it."
questions.explain: A decision made at the moment of speaking uses *will*.

questions.q: I *___* my dentist at 3 o'clock tomorrow — it's all arranged.
questions.explain: Personal arrangements use the present continuous.

questions.q: I'll call you as soon as I *___* home.
questions.explain: After *as soon as, when, if* we use a present tense for the future.

questions.q: By the time you arrive, we *___* dinner.
questions.explain: The future perfect shows something completed before a future time.

questions.q: This soup *___* delicious.
questions.explain: *taste* describing a quality is a state verb, so no continuous.

questions.q: I enjoy *___* in the sea.
questions.explain: *enjoy* is followed by *-ing*.

questions.q: Please remember *___* the lights when you leave.
questions.explain: *remember to do* = don't forget a task; *remember doing* = a memory.

questions.q: We stopped *___* lunch at a little café.
questions.explain: *stop + to-infinitive* = stop in order to do something else.

questions.q: She made me *___* the whole story again.
questions.explain: *make + object + bare infinitive*.

questions.q: This bridge *___* in 1890.
questions.explain: The passive is *be + past participle*; the bridge didn't build anything itself.

questions.q: I'm going to *___* tomorrow.
questions.explain: *have something done* = someone else does it for you.

questions.q: You *___* wear a uniform — it's optional.
questions.explain: *don't have to* = not necessary; *mustn't* = not allowed.

questions.q: She's not answering. She *___* be asleep.
questions.explain: *must* expresses a confident deduction about the present.

questions.q: That *___* be Tom — he's on holiday in Spain.
questions.explain: The negative of a deduction with *must* is *can't*.

questions.q: You *___* told me! I would have helped.
questions.explain: *should have + past participle* criticises or regrets a past action.

questions.q: If I *___* more money, I would buy a new car.
questions.explain: The second conditional uses *if + past simple, would + base form*.

questions.q: If she had left earlier, she *___* the train.
questions.explain: Third conditional: *if + past perfect, would have + past participle*.

questions.q: I wish I *___* speak Japanese.
questions.explain: *wish + could* for an ability we don't have now.

questions.q: Take an umbrella *___* it rains.
questions.explain: *in case* = as a precaution, because it might happen.

questions.q: I can't put up *___* this noise any longer.
questions.explain: *put up with* is a phrasal-prepositional verb meaning *tolerate*.

questions.q: Turn *___*, please.
questions.explain: With a pronoun object, the pronoun goes between the verb and the particle.

questions.q: Can you explain *___*?
questions.explain: *explain something to someone*; the person can't be the direct object.

questions.q: I suggest *___* now.
questions.explain: *suggest (that) + subject + verb*, or *suggest + -ing*; never *suggest someone to*.
